answer: A kernel banks standing only through judged wins: each epoch it locks sable to draw a task from a fixed queue, and only the kernel ranking first takes the win plus opal weight that squares its win count, weight no clone can buy or merge. A fresh clone carries zero influence; to match one honest agent, every clone must win T tasks of its own, forfeiting its locked sable on each loss and burning real compute each try. The queue never stretches, so k clones must beat the live field k·T times — the k-th clone adds T more contested wins. An honest newcomer locks sable once and climbs alone.
